subject: computer-science
title: Algorithms & Flowcharts: Foundations
welcome_lead: An algorithm is a recipe — a step-by-step plan a computer can follow.
meta_desc: KS3 algorithms: step-by-step instructions, flowchart shapes, sequencing.
final_note: Once your plan is clear, the code almost writes itself.

concepts.def: A precise, ordered set of steps to solve a problem.
A diagram showing an algorithm using shapes.
Steps carried out one after another in order.
Oval shape marking the start or end of a flowchart.
Rectangle showing an action or calculation.
Diamond shape asking a yes/no question.

walkthroughs.body_html: An algorithm is a clear list of steps. A recipe is an algorithm. So is a route to school. Each step must be unambiguous — only one meaning.
Use an oval for start/end, a rectangle for a process, a parallelogram for input/output, and a diamond for a decision. Arrows show order.
To trace an algorithm, walk through it with example data and note what changes. This catches bugs before any code is written.
